Population

Distribution Parameters

  • Mean

Estimating the Population Parameters

  • We don’t usually know the true population parameters
  • We have to estimate them based on sampling

The law of large numbers

The law of large numbers

N → ∞   ⇒   X → μ

The more data we have, the closer our parameter estimates get to the true population parameters

Estimating the population mean

Symbol What it’s called Do we know what it is?
X Sample mean Yes - Calculated from the raw data
μ\mu True population mean Almost never known for sure
μ̂\hat{\mu} Estimate of the population mean Yes - Identical to the sample mean

A sample statistic is a description of your data, whereas the estimate is a guess about the population.

Estimating the population standard deviation

s=∑(X−X‾)2N
σ^=∑(X−X‾)2N−1

Bessel’s correction

Estimating the population standard deviation

Symbol What it’s called Do we know what it is?
ss Sample standard deviation Yes - calculated from the raw data
σ\sigma Population standard deviation Almost never known for sure
σ̂\hat{\sigma} Estimate of the population standard deviation Yes - but not the same as the sample standard deviation
s2s^2 Sample variance Yes - calculated from the raw data
σ2\sigma^2 Population variance Almost never known for sure
σ̂2\hat{\sigma}^2 Estimate of the population variance Yes - but not the same as the sample variance

Effect size

What is an effect?

How big is the effect of the independent variable on the dependent variable?

(NOT the same thing as statistical significance!)

Effect Size: Cohen’s d

d̂=θ̂M−θ̂Tσ̂pooled=4.5−3.51.25=0.80\hat{d} = \frac{\hat{\theta}_M - \hat{\theta}_T}{\hat{\sigma}_{\text{pooled}}} = \frac{4.5 - 3.5}{1.25} = 0.80

Measured in standard deviation units

(Frank et al., 2025)

Effect Size: Cohen’s d

Pearson’s r

Covariance

cov(M,A)=E[(M−θM)(A−θA)]\text{cov}(M, A) = E[(M - \theta_M)(A - \theta_A)]

Correlation coefficient

rM,A=cov(M,A)σMσAr_{M,A} = \frac{\text{cov}(M, A)}{\sigma_M \sigma_A}

(Frank et al., 2025)
